in.rationale: The authors argue that Kirchner et al.'s training method inherits the theoretical weaknesses they prove for Anil et al.'s single-message protocol, without rerunning Kirchner et al.'s experiments, so CRITIQUES. They also acknowledge Kirchner et al.'s findings that prover accuracy and verifier robustness improve.
in.scope: proposed CRITIQUES: Choice of interaction protocol for training LLM provers and verifiers; the limitation is theoretical (proof-system strength), not about Kirchner et al.'s legibility measurements

text: The authors alternate between training a verifier and a prover prompted to act helpful or sneaky on disjoint subsets of grade-school math problems with known answers. Each round, the verifier is first trained with supervised learning to predict correctness of solutions from a balanced mixture of previous-round provers, and then the prover is optimized with RL on a reward combining solution correctness and current-round verifier acceptance.
title: Checkability training: alternate verifier supervised learning and helpful/sneaky prover RL
